correctness.rationale: For a full-dimensional integral lattice polygon P with I interior and B≥3 boundary lattice points, Pick gives L_P(n)=(I+B/2−1)n²+(B/2)n+1. For Q=P×[0,m], m≥1, L_Q(n)=(mn+1)L_P(n); conversion to the four-dimensional Ehrhart-series denominator yields coefficients [1,(m+1)(I+B−3)+3m−1,(2m−1)(I+B−3)+(2m+1)I,(m−1)I]. The planar numerator 1+(I+B−3)t+It² has nonreal roots only if B=3,I=1,2,3. For the remaining real-rooted planar bases, the cited Wagner Hadamard/product theorem handles multiplication with [0,m]. For the three exceptional inputs, direct symbolic cubic discriminant expansions in q=m−1 were independently reproduced as [0,288,549,288,0], [256,2304,4180,2832,600], and [2304,10560,16317,10800,2592] (ascending coefficients). All are nonnegative on q≥0 and positive for cubic degree q>0; the q=0 quadratic discriminants are 4(I−1)². Positive nonconstant coefficients exclude nonnegative roots, establishing strict negativity of all roots including multiplicity. This is an infinite argument, not an inference from a finite grid.
